NONE: B2 earth that has been mixed with water
泥，泥土；爛泥，泥漿；淤泥

example: The vehicles got bogged down in the heavy mud.
車輛深陷淤泥，動彈不得。
Modern houses have replaced the one-room mud huts with grass roofs that had been home to generations of peasants.
新式住房取代了農民世代居住的單間草頂土屋。
These mud flats (= level ground near the sea) are a site of special scientific interest.
這片淤泥灘有特殊的科研價值。

NONE: › a small round shape made of mud by children playing
（兒童玩的）泥餅
› said to mean that people are likely to believe something bad that is said about someone, even if it is not true
泥巴黏身不易掉；誹謗總是有人信
C2 an untidy or confused state
混亂狀態；糟糕局面

example: The documents were in a muddle.
檔雜亂地堆在一起。
Whenever I go to Europe I get in a muddle about/over (= become confused about) how much things cost.
我每次歐洲，總是把錢弄得亂糟糟的搞不清。

NONE: › to continue doing something with no clear purpose or plan
混日子，得過且過

example: Decide what you want in life - don't just muddle along.
訂立明確的人生目標——不要混日子過活。

NONE: C2 to think that a person or thing is someone or something else because the two people or things are very similar
混淆

example: I often muddle up Richard with his brother.
我常常分不清理查和他哥哥。
It's easy to muddle up some Spanish and Italian words.
一些西班牙語詞彙和義大利語詞彙很容易互相混淆。

NONE: C2 to arrange things in the wrong order
把…弄亂

example: I've arranged the books alphabetically so don't muddle them up.
我已經把書按字母順序排好了，不要弄亂。

NONE: › to manage to do something although you are not organized and do not know how to do it
胡亂應付過去

example: Sorry, but I can't help you - you'll just have to muddle through on your own.
恐怕我幫不到你——你必須自己設法應付。

NONE: › not thinking clearly or in an organized way
頭腦糊塗的
› badly organized or confusing
混亂的；雜亂無章的
› A person who is muddled is confused
頭腦不清楚的；糊塗的；困惑的

example: a muddled legal situation
混亂的法律形勢
He became increasingly muddled as he grew older.
他年紀越大越糊塗。

NONE: B2 covered by or containing mud (= wet, sticky earth)
泥濘的；渾濁的；黏滿爛泥的
› to put mud (= wet, sticky earth) into something or cover something with mud
使黏上爛泥；使渾濁
› Muddy colours are dark and not bright.
（顏色）灰暗的，暗淡的

example: Don't bring those muddy boots inside!
別把那雙黏滿爛泥的靴子拿進來！
The room has been painted in muddy browns and greens.
客廳漆成灰暗的棕色和綠色。
Industrial activity has muddied the river.
工業生產活動使這條河變得渾濁了。

NONE: › to make a situation more confused and less easy to understand or deal with
把水攪渾，使變得更複雜
› one of the pieces of rubber attached to a vehicle behind the wheels to prevent dirt and small objects from being thrown up
（車輛輪胎的）擋泥板
› a flat area of very wet soil near the sea that is covered at high tide (= the time when the sea reaches its highest level)
淤泥灘，潮泥灘
› a curved piece of metal or plastic above the wheels of a bicycle or motorcycle that prevents dirt from getting on the rider
（腳踏車或機車的）擋泥板
› a special substance that you put on your face and leave for a short time to improve your skin
（美容用的）泥面膜；泥漿面膜
› a mass of mud (= wet earth) moving suddenly and quickly down a steep slope
泥石流
› the act of saying insulting or unfair things about someone, especially to try to damage their reputation
誹謗，中傷

example: political mud-slinging
政治誹謗
